title: Installation
text: The following steps are required to install MAMMA MIA.

title: Installation
text:
Clone the repository
First clone a MAMMA MIA release, it is highly recommended to download the latest one which can be found on the releases page.
$ git clone https://github.com/NOC-MDP/MammaMia/releases/tag/0.4.1
The above command will clone the 0.4.1 release of MAMMA MIA.

title: Installation
text:
Set up python environment
Assuming a conda package manager as a virtual env:
$ conda create -n mm python=3.13 esmpy pyinterp  # these dependancies aren't easily installable via pip
This should create a virtual environment containing python 3.13 which MAMMA MIA is compatible with,
$ conda activate mm
Then you can install MAMMA MIA itself, note the command below must be run in the top level of the MAMMA MIA repository.
$ pip install .

title: Installation
text:
Optional dependancies
By default no simulator is installed alongside MAMMA MIA, this is to simplify the install process as for example the glidersim requires an C++ compiler to install all of its dependencies, and this is an additional complication that may not be required e.g. if the user doesn’t want to simulate a glider. To install MAMMA MIA with the glidersim:
$ pip install '.[glidersim]'
As other simulators become available they will be added here, e.g. parcels for argo float simulation.
To install all simulators (currently just glidersim) then:
$ pip install '.[all]'

title: Simulators
text: We have several types of simulator to use (Slocum gliders are currently the only integrated simulator)

title: Simulators
text:
Slocum Gliders
MAMMA MIA provides a simplified interface with glidersim, it also provides an integration with glidersim providing environmental data like u/v currents and temperature and salinity when it is running a mission simulation.

Mission builder
MAMMA MIA provides an GliderMissionBuilder class that allows users to create Slocum glider missions without having to configure glidersim directly.
There are two missions that can be built (more will be added), a virtual_mooring and follow_waypoints.

Virtual Mooring
The code snippet below shows how to configure and run a virtual mooring mission.
from mamma_mia import GliderMissionBuilder

virtual_mooring = GliderMissionBuilder.virtual_mooring(
    mission_name="rapid-mooring_spiral",
    datetime_str="2023-03-03T12:00:00:Z",
    description="RAPID ARRAY spiral simulation",
    glider_model="DEEP",
    inital_heading=225,
    lat_ini=27.225,
    lon_ini=-15.4225,
    glider_name="comet",
    mission_directory="RAPID-mooring_spiral",
    dive_depth=1000,
    spiral=False
)

virtual_mooring.run_mission(maxSimulationTime=2,verbose=True) # 2 days
virtual_mooring.save_mission()
This snippet creates a virtual mooring mission, starting at midnight on the 3rd March 2023 at 27.225 degrees N and -15.4225 degrees E, diving to 1000 metres.
Then the mission is ran for 2 days and finally saved (important for MAMMA MIA to import the trajectory).
The output will be a NetCDF file that can be specified as input to a MAMMAMIA mission.


Follow Waypoints
The second mission type that can be created is follow_waypoints:
from mamma_mia import GliderMissionBuilder

waypoints = GliderMissionBuilder.follow_waypoints(
    mission_name="waypoints2",
    datetime_str="2023-03-03T12:00:00:Z",
    description="follow waypoints simulation",
    glider_model="DEEP",
    inital_heading=225,
    lat_ini=27.225,
    lon_ini=-15.4225,
    lat_wp=[27.425,27.825,28.205,28.503],
    lon_wp=[-15.4225,-15.4225,-15.4225,-15.4225],
    glider_name="comet",
    mission_directory="waypoints2",
    dive_depth=1000
)

waypoints.run_mission(maxSimulationTime=7,verbose=True) # 7 days
waypoints.save_mission()
This snippet will start at 27.225 degrees N, -15.4225 degrees East and will try and head to the next way point as specified in the lat_wp and lon_wp lists. While doing this will be diving to 1000 metres. Once it reaches the first way point it will then head to the second.
The mission is then run for 7 days, NOTE the glider may not reach all waypoints as that will depend on its ability to travel to them in the time simulated.
Finally the mission is exported and can again be used as input into MAMMAMIA

title: What is Mamma Mia?
text: Back to top

title: Introduction
text:
MAMMA MIA
MAMMA MIA is a platform payload simulator
This toolbox simulates the payload of a platform that is sampling the ocean. Input trajectories have a payload simulated that relates to the sensors on the platform. Optionally the toolbox can also simulate the trajectory of a platform, currently only slocum gliders are supported, although autosubs, argo floats and airborne (observing ocean surface) are expected to be added in future releases.
When give a trajectory (either simulated, from an actual AUV or csv waypoints), the toolbox will search and find the best models to create a world that encompasses the trajectory. The world will hold as much data as can be found that matches the platforms simulated payload.
Each trajectory is defined as a mission, these can be added to a campaign allowing multiple platforms to operate together,these missions can be different platforms e.g. glider and an Autosub or the same platform with different configurations.e.g. same glider with different payloads or the same glider with the same payload but with different model sources set.
When the mission is flown, Mamma Mia will create a simulated data payload of what would be expected from the glider if it had been operated in the real world with model data substituting observations. Some effect is made to match datasets that gliders collect operationally, e.g. different sensor rates can be specified and comparable metadata is generated.

title: Installation
text:
Windows Support
The above process will most likely not work on windows due to dependencies not having pre built binaries available for Windows (e.g. PyInterp, esmpy). While this is surmountable, by building these dependencies, the recommended workaround is to use a docker or similar container containing a linux distribution or Windows Subsystem for Linux.

title: Installation
text:
Optional dependencies
By default no simulator is installed alongside MAMMA MIA, this is to simplify the install process as for example the glidersim requires an C++ compiler to install all of its dependencies, and this is an additional complication that may not be required e.g. if the user doesn’t want to simulate a glider. To install MAMMA MIA with the glidersim:
$ pip install '.[glidersim]'
As other simulators become available they will be added here, e.g. parcels for argo float simulation.
To install all simulators (currently just glidersim) then:
$ pip install '.[all]'

title: usage
text:
MAMMA MIA requires a trajectory that is located in the ocean, this can be from a number of different sources, currently supported sources are:

integrated slocum glider simulator
timeseries NetCDF/Zarr file
way-points in csv file



MAMMA MIA can run simplified missions using the slocum glider simulator, glidersim. If the user installs this optional dependency then glider missions can be ran that will create compatible MAMMA MIA input. The glidersim will also use MAMMA MIA to get environmental data to use during simulation for currents and density etc. glidersim is designed to work exactly like programming an real slocum glider. Therefore MAMMA MIA provides a simplified interface with the current behaviors able to be programmed:

virtual mooring (try to make continuous dives at same point)
follow way-points

Other behaviors/mission will be added or the ability to chain behaviors, e.g. perform virtual mooring for x period then follow way-points to next mooring site etc.
See Simulators section for more information on using the MAMMA MIA interface.



MAMMA MIA can read netcdf or zarr files that contain timeseries data. Examples include BODC netcdf files generated as output from real glider and ALR missions, but any 3D spatial timeseries with time dimension data should work, i.e. it needs, a latitude, longitude, depth and time.



MAMMA MIA can read csv files that contain a set of way points, these must be again 3D (need to specify depth) and contain a suitable time value. MAMMA MIA will linearly interpolate a trajectory from these way points based on the mission time step.



Observation based input datasets, where time is an observation and not a dimension. e.g. PARCELS output datasets.
Surface simulated payloads, MAMMA MIA currently only supports using 3D datasets, and can only interpolate within the model/dataset boundaries. Since most 3D parameters in models have an shallowest depth of around 0.5 metres this means there is no payload simulated when the glider or other platforms are on the surface.
The solution is to use a suitable surface field parameter in these situations, which also means MAMMA MIA will be able to support airborne platforms observing the ocean surface.

MAMMA MIA output contains the following hierarchical structure:

Campaign: contains one or more missions

Missions: contains a single platform deployment with one or more sensors

payload: contains the simulated sensor payload for the deployment

title: Example MAMMA MIA Campaigns
text:
Single glider repeat diving at single point (over RAPID Array mooring) for 2 days, note that uses the output from the glider mission builder. See simulators section for more information on creating these inputs
from mamma_mia import Campaign
from mamma_mia import inventory

# create campaign
campaign = Campaign(name="RAPID array virtual mooring",
                    description="single slocum glider deployment at a RAPID mooring",
                    verbose=True,
                    )
# create platform entity (mutable)
Churchill = inventory.create_platform_entity(entity_name="Churchill",platform_model="Slocum_G2",serial_number="unit_398")

# register sensor to platform
Churchill.register_sensor(sensor_type="CTD")
# register platform to the campaign for use in missions
campaign.register_platform(entity=Churchill)

# # # add mission
campaign.add_mission(mission_name="RAD24_01",
                     title="Churchill with CTD deployment at RAPID array mooring eb1l2n",
                     summary="single glider deployed to perform a virtual mooring flight at the eb1l2n RAPID array.",
                     platform_name="Churchill",
                     trajectory_path="data/RAPID-mooring/rapid-mooring.nc",
                     source_location="CMEMS",
                     mission_time_step=60,
                     apply_obs_error=True)

# build missions (search datasets, download datasets, build interpolators etc)
campaign.build_missions()

# run/fly missions
campaign.run()

# visualise the results
campaign.missions["RAD24_01"].plot_trajectory()
campaign.missions["RAD24_01"].show_payload()

# export to zarr file/store
campaign.export()

section: Replication of existing glider and ALR deployment
text:
Replication of existing glider and ALR deployment
Use real trajectories of the BIOCARBON mission to simulate payloads, they are available from here download the OG netcdf files for each platform.
# This script creates an payload emulation of the BIO-Carbon Deployment

from mamma_mia import Campaign
from mamma_mia import inventory

# create campaign
campaign = Campaign(name="BIO-Carbon",
                    description="This campaign involves the deployment of two Autosub Long Range (ALR) and four gliders "
                                "in the Iceland Basin under the Biological Influence on Future Ocean Storage of Carbon "
                                "(BIO-Carbon) programme, funded by a Natural Environment Research Council (NERC) "
                                "Strategic Research Grant. The gliders were deployed May 2024 and the ALRs were deployed"
                                " in June 2024, with the gliders being deployed from and recovered by the RRS Discovery "
                                "(DY180) alongside four Argo floats, and the ALRs being shore launched.",
                    verbose=True
                    )


# create platform entities
# since the trajectory is from processed output, NMEA_conversion should be false as the conversion has already been applied
Nelson = inventory.create_platform_entity(entity_name="Nelson",
                                          platform_model="Slocum_G2",
                                          serial_number="unit_397",
                                          NMEA_conversion=False)
Doombar = inventory.create_platform_entity(entity_name="Doombar",
                                           platform_model="Slocum_G2",
                                           serial_number="unit_405",
                                           NMEA_conversion=False)
Cabot = inventory.create_platform_entity(entity_name="Cabot",
                                         platform_model="Slocum_G2",
                                         serial_number="unit_345",
                                         NMEA_conversion=False)
ALR4 = inventory.create_platform_entity(entity_name="ALR4",
                                        platform_model="ALR_1500",
                                        serial_number="ALR_4")
ALR6 = inventory.create_platform_entity(entity_name="ALR6",
                                        platform_model="ALR_1500",
                                        serial_number="ALR_6")

# register sensors to platform entities
Nelson.register_sensor(sensor_type="CTD")
Nelson.register_sensor(sensor_type="radiometer")
Nelson.register_sensor(sensor_type="dissolved_gas")

Doombar.register_sensor(sensor_type="CTD")
Doombar.register_sensor(sensor_type="radiometer")
Doombar.register_sensor(sensor_type="dissolved_gas")

ALR4.register_sensor(sensor_type="CTD")
ALR4.register_sensor(sensor_type="dissolved_gas")
ALR4.register_sensor(sensor_type="optical_backscatter")

ALR6.register_sensor(sensor_type="CTD")
ALR6.register_sensor(sensor_type="dissolved_gas")
ALR6.register_sensor(sensor_type="optical_backscatter")


Cabot.register_sensor(sensor_type="CTD")
Cabot.register_sensor(sensor_type="radiometer")
Cabot.register_sensor(sensor_type="dissolved_gas")


# register platforms to the campaign for use in missions
campaign.register_platform(entity=Nelson)
campaign.register_platform(entity=Doombar)
campaign.register_platform(entity=Cabot)
campaign.register_platform(entity=ALR4)
campaign.register_platform(entity=ALR6)

# # add Nelson mission
campaign.add_mission(mission_name="Deployment_646",
                     title="Nelson BIO-Carbon deployment",
                     summary="Nelsons's mission that it undertook during BIO-Carbon",
                     platform_name="Nelson",
                     trajectory_path="BioCarbonTrajectories/Nelson_646_R.nc",
                     creator=creator,
                     publisher=publisher,
                     contributor=contributor,
                     source_location="CMEMS",
                     mission_time_step=60)

# # add Doombar mission
campaign.add_mission(mission_name="Deployment_648",
                     title="Doombar BIO-Carbon deployment",
                     summary="Doombar's mission that it undertook during BIO-Carbon",
                     platform_name="Doombar",
                     trajectory_path="BioCarbonTrajectories/Doombar_648_R.nc",
                     creator=creator,
                     publisher=publisher,
                     contributor=contributor,
                     source_location="CMEMS",
                     mission_time_step=60)

# # add ALR4 mission
campaign.add_mission(mission_name="Deployment_649",
                     title="ALR4 BIO-Carbon deployment",
                     summary="ALR4's mission that it undertook during BIO-Carbon",
                     platform_name="ALR4",
                     trajectory_path="BioCarbonTrajectories/ALR_4_649_R.nc",
                     creator=creator,
                     publisher=publisher,
                     contributor=contributor,
                     source_location="CMEMS",
                     mission_time_step=60)

# # add ALR6 mission
campaign.add_mission(mission_name="Deployment_650",
                     title="ALR6 BIO-Carbon deployment",
                     summary="ALR6's mission that it undertook during BIO-Carbon",
                     platform_name="ALR6",
                     trajectory_path="BioCarbonTrajectories/ALR_6_650_R.nc",
                     creator=creator,
                     publisher=publisher,
                     contributor=contributor,
                     source_location="CMEMS",
                     mission_time_step=60)

# # add Cabot mission
campaign.add_mission(mission_name="Deployment_645",
                     title="Cabot BIO-Carbon deployment",
                     summary="Cabot's mission that it undertook during BIO-Carbon",
                     platform_name="Cabot",
                     trajectory_path="BioCarbonTrajectories/Cabot_645_R.nc",
                     creator=creator,
                     publisher=publisher,
                     contributor=contributor,
                     source_location="CMEMS",
                     mission_time_step=60)

# build missions (search datasets, download datasets, build interpolators etc)

title: configuration
text:
MAMMA MIA uses an internal JSON file to specify its platforms, users can create new platforms by writing their own json file and placing it in the working directory where MAMMA MIA is ran from.


Platforms are specifed in a file called platforms.json. An example file looks like this:
{
    "platforms": [
            {
                "platform_type": "ARGO",
                "platform_model": "APEX",
                "platform_manufacturer": "Teledyne Webb Research",
                "NEMA_coordinate_conversion": false
            },
            {
                "platform_type": "ARGO",
                "platform_model": "ARVOR",
                "platform_manufacturer": "NKE-INSTRUMENTATION",
                "NEMA_coordinate_conversion": false
            }
    ]
}
Here two new platforms are specified, two different models of ARGO floats. Currently there are only 4 fields to specify mostly for meta data purposes, type, model, manufacturer. The final boolean field NEMA_coordinate_conversion specifies if the trajectory coordinates require conversion from NMEA coordinates. This is required if the glider simulator is used as this produces a “raw” file but other sources such as processed NetCDF’s may already be converted.



Sensors are specified using a file called sensors.json. In the example below two sensors are specified for one of the new ARGO float platforms defined above. An CTD and a data logger. A platform requires a data logger to be specified otherwise it cannot load a trajectory. At least one sensor is required as otherwise no payload will be simulated. All sensors have the same structure:

sensor_model: used for meta data purposes
instrument_type: defines instrument type NOTE: this is important as this string is used to find the sensor to add it to the platform.
specification: dictionary containing a set of parameters the sensor is observing. (see specification section)
platform_compatibility: this is a list of platforms that can use this sensor, this must match an specified platform

NOTE: sensors are organised into different sub lists, e.g. CTD and data_logger. These are for help in reading the file and are not used by MAMMA MIA directly.
{
    "sensors": {
        "CTD": [
            {
                "sensor_model": "APEX CTD",
                "instrument_type": "CTD",
                "specification": {
                    "INSITU_TEMPERATURE": {
                        "accuracy": 0.001,
                        "resolution": 0.001,
                        "drift_per_month": 0.0002,
                        "range": [-5, 42],
                        "percent_errors": false,
                        "noise_std": 0.0005,
                        "meta_data": "insitu temperature"
                    },
                    "PRACTICAL_SALINITY": {
                        "accuracy": 0.005,
                        "resolution": 0.0001,
                        "drift_per_month": 0.003,
                        "range": [0, 42],
                        "percent_errors": false,
                        "noise_std": 0.0025,
                        "meta_data": "practical salinity"
                    },
                    "PRESSURE": {
                        "accuracy": 0.1,
                        "resolution": 0.002,
                        "drift_per_month": 0.0042,
                        "range": [0, 2000],
                        "percent_errors": true,
                        "noise_std": 0.0005,
                        "meta_data": "pressure"
                    }
                },
                "platform_compatibility": ["APEX"]
            }
        ],
        "data_logger": [
            {
                "sensor_model": "APEX Data logger",
                "instrument_type": "data_logger",
                "specification": {
                    "DEPTH": {
                        "accuracy": -999.999,
                        "resolution": -999.999,
                        "drift_per_month": -999.999,
                        "range": [-999.999, -999.999],
                        "percent_errors": false,
                        "noise_std": -999.999,
                        "meta_data": "glider_depth"
                    },
                    "LATITUDE": {
                        "accuracy": -999.999,
                        "resolution": -999.999,
                        "drift_per_month": -999.999,
                        "range": [-999.999, -999.999],
                        "percent_errors": false,
                        "noise_std": -999.999,
                        "meta_data": "latitude"
                    },
                    "LONGITUDE": {
                        "accuracy": -999.999,
                        "resolution": -999.999,
                        "drift_per_month": -999.999,
                        "range": [-999.999, -999.999],
                        "percent_errors": false,
                        "noise_std": -999.999,
                        "meta_data": "longitude"
                    },
                    "TIME": {
                        "accuracy": -999.999,
                        "resolution": -999.999,
                        "drift_per_month": -999.999,
                        "range": [-999.999, -999.999],
                        "percent_errors": false,
                        "noise_std": -999.999,
                        "meta_data": "time"
                    }
                },
                "platform_compatibility": ["APEX"]
            }
        ]
    }
}


The specification field in a sensor defines the parameters that the sensor is observing, it also determines the observation error that will be applied to model data to simulate the observation. These values can be used to replicate existing sensors or to simulate entirely new ones. Or if no sensor error simulation is desired then -999.999 can be used as a null/ignore value.
Each parameter in the sensor specification dictionary contains the following:

accuracy: a random value is selected from a uniform distribution of plus/minus this value
resolution: values are rounded to this amount
drift_per_month: this drift rate is applied for all values with start of timeseries assumed to be freshly calibrated
range: values are clipped to this range
percent_errors: if true then accuracy, resolution, drift and noise are assumed to be percentage values
noise_std: sampled random value from a normal distribution with this standard deviation
meta_data:

The process for applying this specification is as follows:

generate accuracy bias values
generate random noise values
calculate drift based on timestep
combine errors by summation and add to timeseries
apply resolution rounding
clip to specified range





Parameters are defined based on their meta data from a vocabulary. There are various collections, MAMMA MIA uses the NERC one here: https://vocab.nerc.ac.uk
Below is an example that has been created to use with the ARGO platform defined earlier. This is a DEPTH parameter, other platforms use other DEPTH parameters such as GLIDER_DEPTH. Parameters are the same in that they are organised into sublists, in this case “navigation” but these are just for readability and not used by MAMMA MIA.
Every parameter has the following fields, most of these are for meta data purposes and come from the vocabulary entry, but some are critical to the operation of MAMMA MIA.

parameter_id: this is the id used within MAMMA MIA for the parameter
identifier: this is the vocabulary reference
vocab_url: the URL where the vocabulary used for this parameter is held
standard_name: short description of parameter
unit of measure: units used for this parameter
unit_identifier: vocabulary reference for the specific units
parameter_definition: longer and more explicit description for the parameter
alternate_sources: If this parameter can be converted from others e.g. pressure from depth, potential_temperature to insitu temperature then they are listed here*
alternate_labels: a different label that the parameter can be known by
source_names: names that parameter can be in source files **

{
    "parameters": {
        "navigation": [
            {
                "parameter_id": "DEPTH",
                "identifier": "SDN:OG1::DEPTH",
                "vocab_url": "https://vocab.nerc.ac.uk/collection/OG1/current/DEPTH/",
                "standard_name": "Depth below sea surface (zero at sea level) of measurement platform",
                "unit_of_measure": "Metres",
                "unit_identifier": "SDN:P06::ULAA",
                "parameter_definition": "Depth below surface of the water body by unknown instrument and correction to zero at sea level using unspecified algorithm.",
                "alternate_sources": [""],
                "alternate_labels": ["DEPTH"],
                "source_names": ["depth"  ,"z"]
            }
        ]
    }
}
* MAMMA MIA needs to know how to convert the parameters for this to work, so only specific conversions are supported. See conversion section
** This is the name of the parameter in any data sources, e.g. potential temperature is often stored as thetao, multiple options can be listed



Some parameters can be converted from one to the other, this often requires other parameters to be present, e.g. temperature conversion also requires depths and salinity. The currently supported conversions are:

potential temperature to insitu temperature
conservative temperature to insitu temperature
absolute salinity to practical salinity
depth to pressure

title: configuration
configuration
text:
Sensors are specified using a file called sensors.json. In the example below two sensors are specified for one of the new ARGO float platforms defined above. An CTD and a data logger. A platform requires a data logger to be specified otherwise it cannot load a trajectory. At least one sensor is required as otherwise no payload will be simulated. All sensors have the same structure:

sensor_model: used for meta data purposes
instrument_type: defines instrument type NOTE: this is important as this string is used to find the sensor to add it to the platform.
specification: dictionary containing a set of parameters the sensor is observing. (see specification section)
platform_compatibility: this is a list of platforms that can use this sensor, this must match an specified platform

NOTE: sensors are organised into different sub lists, e.g. CTD and data_logger. These are for help in reading the file and are not used by MAMMA MIA directly.
{
    "sensors": {
        "CTD": [
            {
                "sensor_model": "APEX CTD",
                "instrument_type": "CTD",
                "specification": {
                    "INSITU_TEMPERATURE": {
                        "accuracy": 0.001,
                        "resolution": 0.001,
                        "drift_per_month": 0.0002,
                        "range": [-5, 42],
                        "percent_errors": false,
                        "noise_std": 0.0005,
                        "meta_data": "insitu temperature"
                    },
                    "PRACTICAL_SALINITY": {
                        "accuracy": 0.005,
                        "resolution": 0.0001,
                        "drift_per_month": 0.003,
                        "range": [0, 42],
                        "percent_errors": false,
                        "noise_std": 0.0025,
                        "meta_data": "practical salinity"
                    },
                    "PRESSURE": {
                        "accuracy": 0.1,
                        "resolution": 0.002,
                        "drift_per_month": 0.0042,
                        "range": [0, 2000],
                        "percent_errors": true,
                        "noise_std": 0.0005,
                        "meta_data": "pressure"
                    }
                },
                "platform_compatibility": ["APEX"]
            }
        ],
        "data_logger": [
            {
                "sensor_model": "APEX Data logger",
                "instrument_type": "data_logger",
                "specification": {
                    "DEPTH": {
                        "accuracy": -999.999,
                        "resolution": -999.999,
                        "drift_per_month": -999.999,
                        "range": [-999.999, -999.999],
                        "percent_errors": false,
                        "noise_std": -999.999,
                        "meta_data": "glider_depth"
                    },
                    "LATITUDE": {
                        "accuracy": -999.999,
                        "resolution": -999.999,
                        "drift_per_month": -999.999,
                        "range": [-999.999, -999.999],
                        "percent_errors": false,
                        "noise_std": -999.999,
                        "meta_data": "latitude"
                    },
                    "LONGITUDE": {
                        "accuracy": -999.999,
                        "resolution": -999.999,
                        "drift_per_month": -999.999,
                        "range": [-999.999, -999.999],
                        "percent_errors": false,
                        "noise_std": -999.999,
                        "meta_data": "longitude"
                    },
                    "TIME": {
                        "accuracy": -999.999,
                        "resolution": -999.999,
                        "drift_per_month": -999.999,
                        "range": [-999.999, -999.999],
                        "percent_errors": false,
                        "noise_std": -999.999,
                        "meta_data": "time"
                    }
                },
                "platform_compatibility": ["APEX"]
            }
        ]
    }
}


The specification field in a sensor defines the parameters that the sensor is observing, it also determines the observation error that will be applied to model data to simulate the observation. These values can be used to replicate existing sensors or to simulate entirely new ones. Or if no sensor error simulation is desired then -999.999 can be used as a null/ignore value.
Each parameter in the sensor specification dictionary contains the following:

accuracy: a random value is selected from a uniform distribution of plus/minus this value
resolution: values are rounded to this amount
drift_per_month: this drift rate is applied for all values with start of timeseries assumed to be freshly calibrated
range: values are clipped to this range
percent_errors: if true then accuracy, resolution, drift and noise are assumed to be percentage values
noise_std: sampled random value from a normal distribution with this standard deviation
meta_data:

The process for applying this specification is as follows:

generate accuracy bias values
generate random noise values
calculate drift based on timestep
combine errors by summation and add to timeseries
apply resolution rounding
clip to specified range

When used as a trajectory input, MAMMAMIA will take these points and linearly interpolate between them based on the requested mission timestep. The snippet below shows an example.
from mamma_mia import Campaign
from mamma_mia import inventory

campaign = Campaign(name="ALR arctic visualisation",
                    description="single ALR capability demo in the arctic",
                    verbose=True
                    )

ALR4 = inventory.create_platform_entity(entity_name="ALR4",
                                        platform="ALR_1500",
                                        serial_number="ALR_4")

ALR4.register_sensor(sensor_type="CTD")

campaign.register_platform(entity=ALR4)

# # add ALR4 mission
campaign.add_mission(mission_name="Arctic Visualisation",
                     title="Under Ice capability demo",
                     summary="",
                     platform_name="ALR4",
                     trajectory_path="arctic_vis_traj.csv",
                     source_location="MSM",
                     mission_time_step=60)

# build missions (search datasets, download datasets, build interpolators etc)
campaign.build_missions()

# run/fly missions
campaign.run()
campaign.missions["Arctic Visualisation"].plot_trajectory()
campaign.missions["Arctic Visualisation"].show_payload()
campaign.export()

campaign.missions["Arctic Visualisation"].export_payload("output2.csv")
